'''Aetintio''', officially the '''Federal Republic of Aetintio''', is a country in [[Western Atirha]]. It is bordered on the east by [[Lasri]], on the north by [[New Misos]], and on the south by the [[Northern Eanif Ocean]]. Aetintio's capital and largest city is [[Elora]]. Aetintio's population in 1765 was estimated to be about [[List of countries and dependencies by population|1.4 million]].

In the beginning of the 16th century, the [[Tavalan Empire]] conquered the [[Atirha|Atirhan]] territory, incorporating it into the [[Grand Colony of New Misos]] ruled from [[Lunava]]. However, the [[Grand Colony]] had little to no influence in the daily affairs of the area, which was colonised in 1400. In 1503, the area was declared the [[Area of Lasri]] by the Tavalans, which included the territory that would become Aetintio until its independence from [[Taval]] in 1583. It was forcibly incorporated into the [[New Misos|New Misos,]] then seceded, joining the [[Federal Republic of United Lasri]] in 1584. When the federation dissolved in 1594, Aetintio became a [[wikipedia:Sovereign_state|sovereign state]]. It then formed a short-lived union with the other members, to [[fight New Misos]], which lasted from 1596 to 1598.

From the late 17th to the mid-18th century, Aetintio endured chronic [[wikipedia:Politics|political]] and [[wikipedia:Economic_stability|economic instability]] characterised by [[wikipedia:Coup_d%27%C3%A9tat|coups]], revolts, and a succession of authoritarian rulers. Persistent [[wikipedia:Economic_inequality|socioeconomic inequality]] and civil unrest culminated in the [[Aetintine Civil War]] from 1710 to 1734, fought between the military-led government and a coalition of [[left-wing guerrilla groups]]. The conflict ended with the [[Loaloer Peace Accords]]. This negotiated settlement established a [[wikipedia:Republic| multiparty constitutional republic]], which remains in place to this day. During the civil war and afterwards, large numbers of Aetintine emigrated to [[Raledria]]. From 1720 to 1740, nearly half a million Aetintine emigrated to [[Raledria]], such that by 1750, they were one of the largest immigrant groups in the eastern half of [[Reledria]].

The economy of Aetintio has historically been dominated by [[agriculture]], beginning with the Tavalans taking control in the 15th century, with production centred in [[Ravika]], along with [[Rlawac]] from the hills. This was followed by a boom in the use of the [[Dwea]] plant in the 16th century, mainly for its use as a dye. Aetintio has since reduced its dependence on [[wikipedia:Dye|dyes]] and embarked on diversifying its economy by opening up trade and financial links and expanding the [[wikipedia:Manufacturing|manufacturing]] sector. The [[Aetintine Sealaq]], the currency of Aetintio since 1592, was replaced by the [[Aetintine Nie]] in 1751. As of 1762 economic improvements had led to Aetintio experiencing the lowest level of [[wikipedia:Income_distribution#Income_inequality|income inequality]] among nearby countries. Among 77 countries included in a 1760 study, Aetintio had one of the least complex economies for doing business.
